title: New CI jobs pin ubuntu-24.04 instead of ubuntu-latest; lightweight jobs use ubuntu-slim
answers: Which runner should a new GitHub Actions job use instead of ubuntu-latest?
Why did MLflow CI stop using ubuntu-latest?
When should a workflow job use ubuntu-slim versus ubuntu-24.04?
How do I avoid the Ubuntu 26.04 migration breaking CI jobs?
body:
Convention: write `runs-on: ubuntu-24.04` explicitly rather than `ubuntu-latest`. GitHub moves `ubuntu-latest` to Ubuntu 26.04 (Oct 19 to Nov 19, 2026), so the label is left unpinned on purpose.
For simple jobs (labeling, commenting, notifications) prefer `runs-on: ubuntu-slim`.
`ubuntu-slim` has a 15-minute timeout, so long-running or polling jobs use `ubuntu-24.04` instead.
Non-Ubuntu runners such as macos-latest are not part of this pin and stay as they are.
Applies to new and edited jobs under .github/workflows/; the style guide is the reference.
applies: GitHub Actions workflow jobs in this repository; not a runtime or test-code rule.
says: Long running automated test jobs are timing out after fifteen minutes on lightweight runners.
Our continuous integration workflow failed because the default cloud operating system version changed.
Run lightweight pull request tasks like labeling and notifications on faster economical runners.
Lock our pull request build checks to a stable operating system release.
search: GitHub Actions workflow jobs under .github/workflows/ must specify runs-on: ubuntu-24.04 explicitly instead of ubuntu-latest, which shifts to Ubuntu 26.04 between Oct 19 and Nov 19, 2026. Simple workflow jobs like labeling, commenting, and notifications prefer runs-on: ubuntu-slim, but long-running or polling jobs must use ubuntu-24.04 because ubuntu-slim has a 15-minute timeout. Non-Ubuntu runners such as macos-latest are not part of this pin and remain unchanged. This convention applies to new and edited jobs under .github/workflows/ according to .claude/skills/github-actions-style/SKILL.md, and does not apply to runtime or test code.
